observation.visible_scene: A wide seascape at twilight: a dark blue-to-black upper sky streaked with pink and magenta clouds, a teal-blue band below them, and a bright orange-yellow glow hugging the horizon. Several low, dark island silhouettes sit on the horizon line (a rounded hill on the left, a small mound near center, a longer ridge on the right). A calm, dark sea fills the lower third, faintly reflecting the warm horizon light with a subtle diagonal shimmer path.
visible_changes: The warm orange-yellow glow at the horizon gradually broadens and brightens across the frame, spreading from a concentrated patch near center-left toward the right side over the excerpt.
The pink/magenta cloud forms in the upper sky show very slow, subtle deformation and drift, with the colored band appearing to thin and shift slightly.
The sea surface continuously ripples, with the texture of the water and the faint reflection path changing from frame to frame.
The island silhouettes and the horizon line remain fixed in position and shape throughout; no object enters or leaves the scene.
No clear camera pan, tilt, or zoom is evident; framing of the islands and horizon stays consistent.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the scene is a sunset or a sunrise, and the full color progression before and after this segment.
The true rate of cloud motion (whether these frames are real-time or time-lapse).
Any change in overall brightness or sky color that occurs beyond the cropped window.
uncertain_details: The apparent cloud 'motion' is minimal over ~2.7 s and may partly reflect compression/grading noise rather than physical drift.
Camera motion cannot be confirmed as zero, but background evidence (static islands/horizon) supports it being negligible.
